20260714_7662148471243148566.t: Learn how to read metric draft marks on a hull, calculate mean draft and trim, differentiate draft from air draft, and ensure adequate under-keel clearance while accounting for squat and tide.

20260716_7663247528988642582.t: A concise guide explaining the essential terminology for every part of a sailboat, including the hull, spars, rigging, and sails.

20260717_7662150223283653910.t: Air draft is the height from the waterline to the vessel's highest fixed point, which varies with cargo, trim, and tide, determining safe clearance under bridges and power cables.

20260719_7662152650045082902.t: Learn how the Plimsoll mark and load line markings indicate maximum draft and freeboard across different water densities and seasonal zones.

20260720_7662153729885408534.t: Understand the crucial distinctions between heel, list, and angle of loll, including why angle of loll is caused by a negative initial metacentric height (GM) and how to safely correct it without capsizing.

20260723_7662159902420389142.t: Learners will understand the definitions, etymologies, memory tricks, and night sidelight color conventions for port and starboard.

20260725_7662162420458212630.t: Learners will understand the main points of sail relative to wind direction, from the no-go zone up to a run, as well as basic port and starboard tack give-way rules.
